title: Garn Meter, our own brainwave model
caption: It follows brainwaves over time and across 14 sensors for an experimental Garn estimate.
alt: Architecture diagram of CorrFuse-EEG, the Garn Meter model, 137,852 parameters. On the left, the real input: a 4-second window of 14 EEG channels, AF3 to AF4, 512 samples each, from a held-out test person in scene 24, divided per channel by its spread in the session's opening 8-second baseline. It passes a convolution with kernel 33 and stride 2, then two convolutions with kernel 5 and stride 2, each channel on its own, giving 56 features by 64 time steps. Then two branches. One: two gated S4D state-space blocks that read time in both directions, then GeM pooling over time after a LayerNorm. Two: a 14 by 14 correlation of the channels' learned features, then an MLP from 105 to 128 to 32 values. A fusion gate joins the 56 and 32 features, then a LayerNorm and an ordinal head with one score s and three learned biases b k. On the right, the real output for this window, an experimental estimate: 0.09 Garn on a scale from 0 to 1, and probabilities 0.37, 0.11 and 0.01 that the person's 1 to 7 discomfort rating is at least 2, 3 and 5. Two equations: the probability that the rating is at least k is the sigmoid of s plus b k; the correlation of channels i and j is the dot product of their learned features divided by the product of their lengths.
